caption:
A reminder from the Qur'an: remember Allah, and He remembers you.

Surah Al-Baqarah (2:152). Swipe through for the Arabic, then English, Mandarin, Korean and Japanese renderings.

Sources on the final slide.

sourcing.arabic: Uthmani script (edition quran-uthmani), api.alquran.cloud. Live-fetched and verified this session (2026-09-11) via GET /v1/ayah/2:152/editions/quran-uthmani,en.sahih,zh.jian,ko.korean,ja.japanese.
sourcing.english: Saheeh International (edition en.sahih), api.alquran.cloud. Same live call as above.
sourcing.chinese: Ma Jian, 马坚 (edition zh.jian), api.alquran.cloud. Same live call as above.
sourcing.korean: Edition ko.korean, api.alquran.cloud. Translator is listed as 'Unknown' in the source's own metadata (englishName field), so the on-slide credit says the same rather than inventing a scholar's name. Same live call as above. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-11 (publishing session): independently re-fetched the same live endpoint and diffed word-for-word against slide-05.json. Four of five languages matched byte-for-byte. The raw API string contains a stray mid-word space ('감 사하고') that slide-05.json renders correctly as one word ('감사하고', gamsahago/'give thanks'); this is a source-data formatting artifact, not a wording change, and matches the same kind of stray-character cleanup already documented for the Korean edition in quran-94-5.meta.json.
sourcing.japanese: Edition ja.japanese, api.alquran.cloud. Translator is listed as 'Unknown' in the source's own metadata, cited on-slide as such. Same live call as above. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-11: matched the re-fetched live response byte-for-byte.
sourcing.verification_note: All five language renderings came from a single live api.alquran.cloud request made this session (2026-09-11), not from memory or a prior file. Response saved to tmp/sourcing-2026-09-11/quran-2-152.json (gitignored scratch, not committed) for this session's own audit trail. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED again in the publishing session later the same day (2026-09-11, via a fresh GET to the identical endpoint): Arabic, English, Chinese and Japanese slide text matched the live API exactly; Korean matched after accounting for a stray source-side space noted above. See channels.json's ig-blankdiscussions._niche_note for why this project treats scripture sourcing as a hard requirement, not a style choice.

renderCommand: npx remotion still src/compositions/registry.tsx IslamicSlide out/blankdiscussions/2026-09-11/quran-2-152-slide-NN.png --props=daily/2026-09-11/blankdiscussions/quran-2-152.slide-NN.json  (run once per slide, NN = 01 through 07)
